subject: Urgent: p95 latency drift for model9b — mitigation plan and SLA exception request
messages:
From: Rajiv Mehra <rajiv.mehra@finvault.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: payments-ops@finvault.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: sudden p95 increase on model9b

Hi Olga,

We started seeing a sustained p95 jump for transaction enrichment calls that hit model9b around 08:30 PT this morning — p95 moved from ~210ms to ~720ms across several hosts. This is impacting our nightly batch reconciliations.

I've attached a small CSV with sample traces and timestamps. Can Redwood confirm whether any model change or infra rollout touched model9b in the last 24 hours? We need an estimate on mitigation steps and an ETA for stabilization.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Mehra | Head of Platform, FinVault

Rajiv — thanks for the heads up and the traces. I'm looping in Marcus (solutions) and Evelyn (SRE) to triage.

Immediate ask: could you confirm whether these requests include long prompt prefixes or unusually long contexts? That helps identify KV-cache or batching behavior.

Planned immediate actions from our side:
- Marcus to check model variant/promotions in the last 24h.
- Evelyn to pull infra-level metrics and check host-level queuing/backpressure.
- If we identify a model-related regression, we'll propose a traffic split to a compatible slower-but-stable variant while we investigate.

I'll follow up with a short mitigation proposal within the hour.

—Olga
Olga Petrov | Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Mehra <rajiv.mehra@finvault.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase on model9b

Hi team — quick summary of what I see from the model catalog and rollout logs:
- No full model version promotion in the last 48h, but we did push an optimized tokenization micro-patch to the v9b-serving stack at ~03:20 PT (non-weight update).
- Telemetry shows a small increase in median sequence length for FinVault traffic (from 180 tokens to ~240 tokens) which increases KV cache churn.

Proposed mitigation (short window):
1) Immediate traffic steering: shift 35% of FinVault production traffic to model9b-quant (quantized variant) which has slightly higher median latency but much lower variance; expected p95 reduction ~30-40%. Requires FinVault sign-off for a temporary SLA carve.
2) Enable prefix caching for the top 25 prompts (we have a candidate list from last quarter) to reduce redundant compute.
3) Collect detailed traces for 6 hours and then reassess for a targeted patch or rollback target.

Risk/notes:
- Quantized variant may slightly change embeddings and exact token-by-token output. For enrichment workloads this is low risk but flagging for the team.
- If we steer traffic, we'll add a short-lived acceptance window and have an automatic fallback if error-rate or 99th rises.

Attachments: link to live dashboard below.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/model9b/latency?range=24h

From: Rajiv Mehra <rajiv.mehra@finvault.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: payments-ops@finvault.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase on model9b

Thanks Marcus — that plan sounds reasonable provided we get:
- A clear DoD (definition of done) for the mitigation and an automatic rollback criterion. We can't accept output drift that materially affects downstream reconciliation results without a sign-off window.
- A telemetry capture that includes input payloads (anonymized) for our compliance team.

For sign-off: FinVault accepts a temporary traffic split to the quantized variant for up to 48 hours under the following conditions:
- Redwood must monitor token-level differences and surface any >0.5% change in reconciliation match rate within the first 6 hours.
- If match rate delta >0.5% or error-rate >0.2%, revert immediately.
- Maintain full audit logs for this activity and share them with payments-ops.

Please confirm whether Redwood can meet those constraints and provide an ETA to enact the split.

Rajiv
Rajiv Mehra | Head of Platform, FinVault

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Mehra <rajiv.mehra@finvault.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase on model9b

Rajiv — agreed on the constraints. Finalizing the plan and next steps: 

Action plan (summary):
- 16:55 PT: start a 35% traffic split to model9b-quant (temporary).
- 16:55–22:55 PT: continuous monitoring window (6 hours primary; extended to 48 hours if stable).
- Telemetry: we will capture anonymized inputs (hash + metadata), per-token diffs, match-rate delta, and full audit logs. Logs and a short daily summary will be shared to payments-ops.
- Roll criteria: revert immediately if match-rate delta >0.5% OR error-rate >0.2% OR 99th latency increases >100ms compared to baseline.
- Post-window: run a joint RCA and propose either a targeted micro-patch or permanent traffic policy change.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_finVault_v1.docx (contains the written SoW and acceptance criteria). HubSpot deal link included for tracking.

Please reply with a single-line sign-off from FinVault to proceed with the split at 16:55 PT. We'll hold until we receive your confirmation.

Thanks — Olga
